title: Raisin and Brown Sugar Steel-Cut Oatmeal
changes_from_base: Steel-cut oats are toasted in butter, simmered in water for a chewier, nuttier porridge, and finished with raisins, light brown sugar and cinnamon instead of milk, banana and blueberries.
summary: Plump raisins and warm brown sugar give this toasted steel-cut oatmeal the comfort-food appeal of a favourite warm pudding.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Melt 14 g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, add 175 g steel-cut oats and toast, stirring, about 2 min until fragrant and golden.

steps.title: Water
steps.text: Pour in 960 ml water and bring to the boil.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Reduce to a gentle simmer over medium-low and cook about 20 min, stirring now and then so it does not catch, until creamy but chewy.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in ¼ tsp salt, cover and rest 5 min.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in 75 g raisins, 38 g light brown sugar and ¼ tsp cinnamon, seasoning with a little more salt to taste.

tips: Toasting the oats before cooking brings out their nuttiness and improves the final texture.
The oatmeal will thicken further as it cools, so stop cooking when it still looks slightly loose.
Stir in raisins after cooking so they stay plump rather than breaking down.
storage: Serve warm; leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days and reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of water or milk. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
